## Observations
1. For person \(j\), the source bib is \(Q_j\), and the bib of the person they stare at is \(Q_{P_j}\).
2. The bib numbers form a permutation of \(1,\ldots,N\), so each answer position is filled exactly once.
3. The answers must be printed in bib-number order, not person-number order.

## Solution sketch
1. > For person \(j\), the source bib is \(Q_j\), and the bib of the person they stare at is \(Q_{P_j}\).

   Read \(N\), \(P\), and \(Q\), and treat the two input sequences as one-indexed. This makes \(P_j\) directly usable as an index into \(Q\).

2. > The bib numbers form a permutation of \(1,\ldots,N\), so each answer position is filled exactly once.

   Allocate a one-indexed answer array \(S\). Visit each person \(j\) once and set \(S_{Q_j}=Q_{P_j}\). No inverse mapping or chain traversal is needed. If a person stares at themselves, the same assignment correctly puts their own bib number in their answer position.

3. > The answers must be printed in bib-number order, not person-number order.

   Print \(S_1,\ldots,S_N\) on one line, separated by single spaces. Reading, filling, and printing the arrays take \(O(N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
